By default it tries googledownloads.cn, the Tencent Cloud mirror and dl.google.com in turn; the download is about 1.8 GB and resumes if interrupted; it verifies the archive, version and platform, then installs into sdk/ keeping execute permissions. It refuses while the SDK is in use, so close the processes using it first. These two only prepare files; this macOS version does not yet support installing or removing them in an instance. source shows or changes the remembered download source (auto, googledownloads_cn, tencent, google); --mirror or --mirror-url overrides the choice for this run. With --json, --accept-license is required (fetch only) and means you accept all licenses of the components to download. Exit codes: license not accepted is 2 (license_declined), not ready or pre-check failed is 4, SDK in use or fetch in progress is 5, download unavailable or verification failed is 9.

status (default) shows the components, same as the components in check. fetch fills in the missing components: it first gets the full text of the Android Software Development Kit License Agreement from the mirror and shows it; only y continues, otherwise nothing is downloaded. It then tries googledownloads.cn, the Tencent Cloud mirror and dl.google.com in turn, downloads the missing adb and system image (about 1.5 GB, resumes if interrupted), verifies them and installs into sdk\. Components that are already complete are skipped; an incomplete old folder is renamed to <folder>.incomplete-<time> and kept, not deleted. --play-store also adds the optional Google Play Store (needed by playstore <i> install; skipped if already present): it downloads the Google Play system image, takes only the five files for the Store, Play services, GSF, partner setup and the Store certificate from its system.img, verifies their SHA-256, puts them in sdk\playstore, and deletes the extracted image and the downloaded archive right away, keeping only those five files. import-playstore fills it in with your own files, without downloading or asking for the license: give Google's official Google Play system image archive (x86_64-34_r14.zip, any name; size and SHA-1 are checked against Google's repository manifest) or the five files themselves (any name; size and SHA-256 are checked one by one; for a folder it takes the files with the matching names inside); anything unrecognized or not matching is rejected and nothing is changed; your files are only read, never touched. status lists whether the five files are present and where they came from (download / import), and does not count them as required components. With no argument it shows the components; source shows or changes the remembered download source (auto, googledownloads_cn, tencent, google). With --json, --accept-license is required (fetch only). Only Windows has a component list; darwin and linux return unsupported. Exit codes: license not accepted is 2 (license_declined); a path with Chinese characters, not enough space, or not a ModAVD folder is 4; fetch in progress is 5; download failed is 9 (components_unavailable); failing verification after download or extraction, or a rejected imported file, is also 9 (components_rejected; error.details.reason in --json is unknown_file, mismatch or incomplete).
status：offline 已关机 / starting 开机中 / onli: status: offline = shut down / starting = booting / online = running / creating = being created / create_failed = creation failed; running tells whether the qemu process exists, booted whether Android has finished booting (both can be true while creating; go by status); busy means another modavd is starting (starting) or shutting down (stopping) it, and it also reports stopping when it is shutting itself down (window closed, shut down inside Android); while creating, creation_progress is the percent done (0-100, counted by finished steps).

trim：在客体的数据盘（/data）上触发一次回收（FITRIM，经 vold: trim: triggers a reclaim (FITRIM, via vold idle maintenance) on the guest's data disk (/data), so the emulator releases the space that deleted files still occupy in the data disk image. The instance must be running and fully booted; success only means it was triggered, it does not wait for the guest to finish reclaiming nor confirm that it worked. If the emulator is too old or the data disk does not support reclaiming, it returns unsupported (exit code 4) instead of running in vain. info: reports the data disk's logical size, the space it actually uses on the host, and (when the instance is shut down) the allocated size and an estimate of how much can be reclaimed; while the instance is running, the allocated and reclaimable numbers are only available after shutdown; read-only, changes nothing. compact: with the instance shut down, rewrites the data disk overlay, drops the freed clusters and shrinks the file; after conversion it verifies (check + compare) before replacing atomically, and the original disk is untouched until the replacement succeeds; refused if the instance has snapshots.

Memory and core count must be one of the listed values; they are not rounded. %vAfter the files are created, it starts headless once in the background, does the post-boot setup, host input method, initial setup and the arm64 execution bridge (only effective for games in the built-in list; other apps are unchanged; --no-bridge skips it, and it is not installed later either), then syncs and shuts down normally. This usually takes a few minutes and progress is printed step by step ("Creating 35%", counted by finished steps); after that the first start is as fast as usual. The new instance has no Google Play Store; if you want it, add it after creation with playstore <i> install. During this time the instance's state is creating (creation_progress in status and list is the percent), and it cannot be started, changed or deleted; if it fails (or is interrupted) it is create_failed, and you redo the initial setup with create --resume N, or delete it with delete N --yes. --count N creates N at once: it first takes N free numbers (none is created when there are fewer), then creates them one by one in number order with the same other options; with --title the names get a number ("T 1", "T 2" …). Before each one the free space of the instances' disk is checked, and below what a start needs it stops and the rest are not created. One failing does not stop the next; the result has results and failed, and when something failed the exit code is that of the first failure.

They are installed in the writable system image overlay that the execution bridge brings, so the instance needs the execution bridge. install puts in the Store and the Google-signed Play services, GSF and partner setup, hides the placeholder apps of the same names in the image, and then cold-starts once to take effect; uninstall removes the updates installed by Google Play and deletes these files, and the placeholder apps return after a cold start. If install fails midway, the files put in during this run are rolled back; if they cannot be fully removed, it is recorded as partly installed (play_store_partial in list), and you remove it with uninstall or complete it with install again. status: read-only, the instance must be running. gsfid: gets this instance's GSF ID (decimal and hex; --json has decimal, hex); if the device is not certified by Play Protect, register it at %v; the instance must be running, and if there is no ID yet it reports not_ready (details.reason is no_gsf_id), so stay online for a minute or two and try again. Without the execution bridge it reports not_ready (details.reason is no_bridge). An instance with the Store installed cannot have its execution bridge removed; remove the Store first. 实验功能。有的游戏在清单里要求 GLES 3.2，Play 商店按实例报的版本把: Experimental. Some games require GLES 3.2 in their manifest, and the Play Store judges ModAVD (which reports 3.1) as incompatible by the version the instance reports. on reports ro.opengles.version as 196610 (3.2) so the Store lets them through; actual rendering is still 3.1, so games that use Vulkan work, while apps that really need GLES 3.2 rendering install but do not open. Off by default, per instance. It works by editing /vendor/build.prop in the writable system image overlay that the execution bridge brings, so the instance needs the execution bridge; without it, it reports not_ready (details.reason is gles32_no_bridge). After the change it cold-starts once to take effect, then checks the version the instance reports and fails if it does not match. If the instance was shut down, it is shut down again afterwards (also when it did not succeed); if it was running, it is started again after the cold start the way it was (with window or headless). status: read-only, the instance must be running; the four values are on, off, pending-on and pending-off (the last two mean no cold start yet). An instance that is running cannot have its execution bridge removed; turn this off first. For an instance with the Google Play Store installed, the Store remembers the old device information: go to Settings → Apps → Google Play Store → Storage and clear the data (the account stays signed in). gles32 in list / info is the record of the switch.

按管理器「设置」里选的更新源（GitHub 或 Mirror 酱，Mirror: Uses the update source chosen in the manager's "Settings" (GitHub or MirrorChyan; downloading from MirrorChyan needs a CDK); a caller with its own settings passes this run's with --source and --cdk-dpapi, which only override "Settings" and are not saved; source and cdk_set in status are the ones in effect for this run. --cdk-dpapi is the base64 of the CDK encrypted with Windows DPAPI; if it cannot be decrypted or the format is wrong it is invalid_argument, and the CDK never goes into logs or output. It does not go online by itself and only does the step you give: status (default) only looks locally; check looks up the latest version; prepare downloads, verifies against the manifest and stages, even while instances are running; install runs prepare first if needed, then puts in sdk\emulator and the other files of the package, and requires all instances, the manager (including in the tray) and MCP clients to be closed first; recover finishes or rolls back an install that was not completed. It uses the same .update folder as AUTO-MAS and can continue what the other side did not finish. --automas-version is the caller's AUTO-MAS version; if the new version needs a newer AUTO-MAS, it is not installed. --after-pid, --reopen, --reopen-arg and --handoff-id are used when "Update" is clicked in the manager's "Settings": the manager downloads and verifies, closes the instances, starts this command and exits; the command waits for it to exit, puts the new version in place, and then reopens the manager. On macOS, --package ZIP --sha256 HEX prepares or installs a local full signed package; the digest must be obtained independently from a trusted source. With --json, each progress step adds a progress object to the log line on stderr (one line each when checking, extracting, verifying and installing start, with percent -1; downloading carries real progress from its first line, then about one line every 2 seconds, and always one when the download finishes): {"stage":"checking|downloading|extracting|verifying|installing","percent":-1 or 0-100,"done_bytes":N,"total_bytes":N}. Being unable to check is exit code 9 (update_unavailable), a download that fails verification is also 9 (update_rejected), and a program in use is 5.

The first start also does the initial setup. Ctrl+C or --timeout only stop waiting: the emulator is not ended and keeps booting. Running start again afterwards takes it over and completes the setup of this start that was not finished (including the initial setup and guest library patches). If the instance is already running and all setup is done, only the setup done on every start is redone. Before returning it confirms that /sdcard can be written to (normally it is long ready by then and costs no time; it waits up to 60 more seconds, and at the deadline only warns). If the instance does not have the arm64 execution bridge yet, it is installed automatically after the setup (one or two shutdown and start rounds in between); --no-bridge skips it this time, and it is not installed for instances where bridge uninstall was used or that were created with --no-bridge, nor when taking over an already running instance.
